characters.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Edit target: the attached pixel art portrait of character K.
Create a production animation sprite sheet for this EXACT portrait, with SIX frames arranged in an EXACT 3-column by 2-row regular grid, no gutters, all cells equal square dimensions. Target canvas 1536 by 1024, each cell 512 by 512.
Duplicate the reference portrait identically into all six cells. Each cell shows the full original teal frame including its irregular decorative bottom edge, the letter K, background, identical glasses, hair, face proportions, outfit, lighting, muted palette, and same pixel-art blocks. Leave outside the teal portrait border transparent. Preserve the framing and exact relative landmark positions of the reference. No head translation, no new facial hair, no new details, no extra lettering.
ONLY animate the mouth and (in the last frame) the eyelids. Talking phonemes, reading order left-to-right then top-to-bottom:
1: original relaxed closed mouth.
2: slightly open mouth for quiet speech, small dark opening.
3: wider open mouth for A, modest mouth, restrained teeth if appropriate.
4: small rounded O mouth, clearly different from frame 2.
5: medium-width mouth for E, subtle thin upper teeth.
6: relaxed closed mouth and a natural eye blink behind the glasses, glasses unchanged.
Each mouth must fit the face angle and existing lip shading. Human casual speech, not shouting, no exaggerated smile. All six bodies, frames and backgrounds must be identical so they can be cropped into a stable animated GIF. Crisp LOW RESOLUTION pixel art matching the source, not smooth illustration, no anti-aliased vector style, no added borders or labels, no checkerboard drawn into the image.
